If you're a stylus lover, then there haven't been many great options when it comes to Android phones as of late. Sure, the pricey Samsung S26 Ultra comes with a built-in S Pen, but if you're after something much cheaper, you might assume that you're out of luck.

Thankfully, Motorola has you covered with the Moto Stylus – one of the few budget-friendly models that comes with a pen. Now, the handset is cheaper than it's ever been on Amazon, with a Black Friday discount that takes it down to just $199.99 from $399.99.

🐲 Chipset: Snapdragon 6 Gen 3🐄 RAM: 8GB💾 Storage: 256GB🔋 Battery: 5,000mAh⭐ Star feature: Built-in stylus.

Despite the low price, it's not a low-end phone by any means. It's got a bright AMOLED display at a butter-smooth 120Hz refresh rate, 8GB of RAM, and (in the case of this particular unit) 256GB of built-in storage. It's powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 6 Gen 3, which, while firmly a mid-range chip, delivers smooth day-to-day performance and casual gaming.

The real start of the show is that stylus, though, and you can pop it out for easy sketching or note-taking. Oh, and the phone is a cool textured blue color, helping it really stand out from the crowd.

A decent mid-range phone that stands out thanks to its included stylus and current low price. This is the cheapest this model has ever been on Amazon, and a killer price for something with a decent chipset, 8GB of RAM, and 256GB of storage. There's also a microSD card slot, so you can add more room if you need it.

✅Recommended if: The Motorola Moto G Stylus is one of the few phone models that come with a built-in stylus and doesn't cost a fortune. If you're looking for a more affordable phone that lets you draw and take notes easily, then the Moto G Stylus is a serious contender.

❌Skip this deal if: You are concerned about the patch support. This 2025 model only comes with two major OS upgrades (though Motorola has at least promised three years of security patches).

This isn't too unreasonable at this ridiculously low price, but if you're the kind of person who really cares about getting the latest updates over the long term, you should consider buying something else.

Tech Report: AI features could be turned off with a simple toggle, Canva proves

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (323 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI has taken over everything in the past few years, with AI features bombarding virtually every app or service available.
  • Canva today confirmed “AI Controls,” a new toggle that completely turns off generative AI features within the editing app.
  • Recent findings suggest that generative AI can be quite helpful in working on posters, editing images, and more, but it’s not everyone’s preference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI has taken over everything in the past few years, with AI features bombarding virtually every app or service available. If you’ve ever wanted to just turn off AI features, Canva proves that it could be a simple toggle, if companies actually wanted to give you a choice.

Canva today confirmed “AI Controls,” a new toggle that completely turns off generative AI features within the editing app.

Recent findings suggest that generative AI can be quite helpful in working on posters, editing images, and more, but it’s not everyone’s preference. Canva puts this well:.

Recent findings suggest that for some people, AI is the most exciting creative tool in a generation, while others prefer bringing their ideas to life without it. We believe the future of creativity should give everyone the freedom to choose their own path, whether that’s creating with AI, without it, or somewhere in between.

Recent findings suggest that to give its customers the choice, Canva’s Permissions menu now has a simple toggle for “Enable Generative AI features.” Toggling it off disables features such as Magic Write and Magic Edit. There’s also an option to limit how much AI-generated imagery appears in the Canva library.

Put simply, this is great to see.

AI has its place, but everyone should have a choice like this, especially when it comes to apps and services used for artistry in the same vein as Canva. Yet, the tech industry continues to go in the opposite direction, shoving AI into every corner whether it’s actually useful or not. Canva proves, though, that it doesn’t have to be that way.

#2760. Tidal is banning fully AI-generated music. Heres how other streaming services compare.

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (731 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Tidal is banning fully AI-generated music. Heres how other streaming services compare.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (731 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, music streaming services add thousands of latest songs every day, and a growing share of them are made entirely with AI.
  • 9, Tidal will begin to remove all fully AI-generated songs from its catalog and block fresh uploads.
  • In a recent development, "We are the first DSP to do so, and we encourage our peers to follow suit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, music streaming services add thousands of latest songs every day, and a growing share of them are made entirely with AI. Some apps have started labeling those tracks or keeping them out of recommendations.

Starting Dec. 9, Tidal will begin to remove all fully AI-generated songs from its catalog and block fresh uploads. Robert Andersen, who leads Tidal at parent firm Block, expects about 29 million tracks to come down by the start of 2027.

In a recent development, "We are the first DSP to do so, and we encourage our peers to follow suit. TIDAL will continue to make decisions that support real artists first," Andersen wrote in a post on X. (DSP stands for digital service provider, which is a platform that streams or sells music — like Spotify, Apple Music, or Deezer.).

Tidal started labeling tracks as "wholly" AI-generated and cutting off royalties back in July. It also moved to take down songs linked to fraud, including artist impersonation. But, according to the service, the uploads kept coming. Tidal flagged 43 percent of the tracks it received over the past 90 days as fully AI-generated, and Andersen estimates the service will turn away 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day once the ban takes effect.

In a recent development, most of those songs go unheard (thankfully). Tidal has already tagged about 27 million tracks as fully AI-generated, roughly 6.3 percent of its catalog. The company says 96 percent of those tracks went unplayed over the past three months.

Some listeners treated the ban as a reason to stick with Tidal or switch to it. "I’m genuinely so happy to have switched from Spotify to this," one commenter wrote in the subreddit, r/TIdaL. On X, another tagged Spotify and asked, "yours when?".

Other replies zeroed in on the word "wholly." One user joked that AI artists would start hiring someone "just to clap on beat." Another asked, "so 1 real cough in the intro and it’s allowed?" Behind the jokes was a practical question for Tidal: how much human input makes a recording AI-assisted?

Even some people who liked the policy wondered how Tidal would enforce it. "Fair play to Tidal, no idea how they’re going to actually catch it all though," wrote one X user. That's the challenge facing the service once it starts deciding which tracks can stay and which come down.

Apple Music is relying on labels and distributors to disclose how AI was used. Its current delivery specifications include tags for cases where AI generated a significant part of a recording, composition, music video, or artwork. A separate tag covers AI-generated artist personas that could pass for real people. In August, Apple told its music partners that the disclosures would become mandatory and that listeners would see a "Made With AI" label later in the year. (What gets labeled depends on what labels and distributors report when they submit the music.).

Industry observers note that deezer uses its own detection tool to label tracks that are fully AI-generated and keep them out of algorithmic recommendations and editorial playlists. In July, the organization also noted it would take down AI tracks used to rack up fraudulent streams or left unplayed for at least six months. Other AI tracks can still turn up in searches, but Deezer says it aims to give listeners a switch to hide them by the end of the year. The company says it receives nearly 90,000 fully AI-generated tracks a day.

According to recent reports, bandcamp put a broader ban in place in January. Its policy covers music and audio made entirely or in substantial part with generative AI, and it also prohibits the use of AI to impersonate artists or their styles.

From YouTubers and TikTok stars to streamers and podcasters, Mashable talks to creators about how they built their platforms, the gear they swear by, and the trends they see coming next.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there’s a familiar interruption that comes with shopping online: you’ve found what you want, you’re ready to check out, and the store asks you to sign in. Was this the account with your usual password? Did you change it last time? Is it easier to reset it again?

For Black Friday, Proton Pass Plus and Pass Family are both 60% off their regular monthly pricing with a one-year subscription, while Proton Unlimited is 50% off. Pass Plus starts at $1.99 per month, billed annually, making this a good opportunity to get your passwords — and a few other important parts of your digital life — organized.

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

Sources indicate that unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

With unlimited logins and encrypted vaults that sync across devices, Proton Pass lets you keep those details together as you move between your phone and computer.

Proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. This makes it trivially easy to access your passwords, passkeys, and API credentials wherever you find yourself.

Black Friday shopping often leaves something behind long after the packages arrive: a steady stream of promotional emails from stores you barely remember visiting.

Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

Recent findings suggest that an alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

Recent findings suggest that if that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to upgrade all your other accounts.

According to recent reports, it’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

Passwords are only part of what’s worth keeping in a secure, accessible place.

Proton Pass also stores notes, credit card details, and other confidential information in end-to-end encrypted vaults. That makes it useful for the small, everyday moments when you need something sensitive and don’t want to go looking for it.

When you’re booking a flight, saved passport details let you look up the information you need without digging through a drawer halfway through the reservation.

When you’re shopping online, saved card details mean you don’t have to leave the checkout page to find your wallet.

When you’re traveling, keeping a digital copy of an crucial document within reach gives you a convenient reference while you’re away from home. It doesn’t replace an original document where one is required, but it can save you from searching through scattered files and messages.

In a recent development, pass Plus also includes a built-in two-factor authenticator, Dark Web Monitoring, and secure link and vault sharing. Those features give you more ways to manage access to your accounts and share sensitive information when you need to.

Pass Plus is the straightforward choice for one person who wants password generation, autofill, unlimited aliases, and secure storage.

According to recent reports, pass Family includes six Pass Plus accounts and a family admin panel. If several people in your household need a password manager, it’s worth considering rather than setting everyone up with separate subscriptions.

In a recent development, in addition to macOS 27.3 beta 2, Apple is also rolling out the first Release Candidates for macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4. Here are the details.

Two weeks ago, Apple released macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, along with macOS 27.2.1 Golden Gate, all of which included security fixes related to AirPlay, Bluetooth, and Messages, among others.

Today, the organization released the first RCs for macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4, along with the second developer beta for macOS 27.3.

As is usually the case with direct-to-RC rollouts, Apple’s notes mention only that the updates provide ”security fixes for your Mac.” The actual release notes will likely become available soon after Apple officially releases macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4 in the coming weeks.

Industry observers note that jokes aside, the Galaxy S26 FE is still a darn good phone for its price. Black Friday is roughly a week away, and Amazon's already knocked the phone down by 25%.

Industry observers note that samsung's latest FE model—the Galaxy S26 FE—is down 25%, dropping its price from $799 to $599. The phone comes with 256GB of storage, the latest Android 17 (One UI 9) software, and Galaxy AI.

If you're asking us, the Galaxy S26 FE is ✅ recommended if you want the latest tech on a budget. Keep in mind that the S26 FE is $799, but with this 25% deal, you'll get it for $599. One UI 9 (Android 17) is another plus, with various UI updates, smoother animations, and AI privacy alerts. Samsung will also support the Galaxy S26 FE with seven years of OS upgrades.

You should probably ❌ skip this deal if you're looking for a more robust phone. The Galaxy S26 FE is a mid-range phone, so its performance isn't top-tier. The phone features Samsung's Exynos 2500 SoC, and while the chip has improved over previous iterations, it may still struggle graphically. What's more, the S26 FE's camera system pales in comparison to Samsung's flagships, as its main highlight is a 50MP main sensor.

According to recent reports, all in all, the Galaxy S26 FE is still a solid buy at 25% off. Samsung introduced the phone this year at a price $50 higher than in previous years. So, seeing it at this discounted price is all the more enticing. Another thing to remember is that the phone's screen size matches the Galaxy S26 Plus—a flagship phone. Samsung tried to bridge the best of both worlds (midrange and flagship), and it does that fairly well.

There are some caveats, but with 256GB of internal storage and a 120Hz display refresh rate, the S26 FE's early Black Friday deal isn't that bad.

  • In a recent development, trump celebrated and claimed credit after Huang was reinstated by the Nvidia board on Monday, a stunning return to power for the embattled CEO.
  • But Trump's jubilation stands in stark contrast to the reaction from even his staunchest allies on Capitol Hill, who recoiled after the reinstatement and vowed to continue their investigations into Huang — whose relationship with a potential Chinese intelligence asset they fear may have jeopardized U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, president Donald Trump wanted Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia. Now that the chip mogul is reinstated, Trump is cheering alone in Washington.

In a recent development, trump celebrated and claimed credit after Huang was reinstated by the Nvidia board on Monday, a stunning return to power for the embattled CEO. In a nearly hourlong phone call with CNBC, the president went as far as saying he "made the deal" to bring Huang back.

But Trump's jubilation stands in stark contrast to the reaction from even his staunchest allies on Capitol Hill, who recoiled after the reinstatement and vowed to continue their investigations into Huang — whose relationship with a potential Chinese intelligence asset they fear may have jeopardized U.S. national security.

"The risk remains that there could be information that a Chinese spy knows about a key individual in the supply chain, and that's not worth the risk," Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said Tuesday on CNBC's "Squawk Box." "We might even have to put a babysitter on Jensen Huang for crying out loud ... just to make sure that he doesn't do something that's going to risk the United States.".

Trump's rare isolation from his party over Huang comes after the GOP was throttled in the midterm elections, as Democrats rode a blue tsunami to capture the Senate and the largest House majority this century. And it suggests Republicans, who have spent a decade in lockstep with the president, may have found an matter on which they can't bring themselves to take Trump's side.

Recent findings suggest that "I can accept what the president has done," Cramer said. "But we have to put guardrails around to protect the United States of America.".

Many midterm voters identified Silicon Valley's most visible outputs, artificial intelligence and data centers, as top concerns motivating them to cast ballots for Democrats. The CNBC All-America Economic Survey in October found 63% of registered voters oppose an AI data center within 10 miles of their home, while just 13% support one.

By timing his extraordinary intervention in Nvidia so soon after the GOP's historic losses, Trump could spark a national debate about corporate governance and responsibility, former Under Secretary of State Richard Stengel remarked.

"With the repudiation of Trumpism in the midterms and voter revulsion with corruption, I think there will be a turn back to a more value-based duty of care for boards of directors and away from the current maximization of shareholder value," Stengel told CNBC in an email.

In a recent development, "Directors are citizens first, shareholders second. The idea that you put profit above national security should disgust shareholders, not please them," Stengel, who worked in the Obama administration, wrote.

Bipartisan lawmakers are now racing to pass a series of export control bills before the year ends, a call that has only grown louder since Huang was reinstated.

There's "not just frustration or political worry, but actual, substantive national security concern here from Democrats and Republicans," Chris McGuire, senior fellow for China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, told CNBC.

Sources indicate that "This has historically been a bipartisan glitch," McGuire said. "Democrats and Republicans generally pretty much agree that we shouldn't be sending our most advanced chips to China.".

According to recent reports, "If it happened in massive quantities, people want to know why, how, and they want to make sure that it doesn't happen again," he said. "And putting your thumb on the scale in this clear of a way seems like it could undercut those efforts.".

The White House didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the political dynamics of Trump's involvement in reinstating Huang.

Republicans will have the first crack at investigating Huang next week before ceding power to Democrats in January. Democrats have vowed their own investigations into the Nvidia CEO and his ties to the president and his Cabinet. The Democrats who will lead those investigations are now hopeful that Republicans will join them.

"I've been seeing a lot of Republicans outraged and scandalized by what has just happened," House Judiciary Committee ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., remarked Tuesday on "Squawk Box," when asked if Republicans may support a bipartisan investigation of Nvidia.

"When else in American history can you think of a time when a president of the United States called up a corporate board of directors meeting and then essentially dictated to them who was going to be their new CEO right after they had fired the guy?".

Industry observers note that trump throughout his second term has stated repeatedly that achieving AI dominance is required for the U.S. to maintain global superiority. His administration has championed the rapid growth of the country's tech giants and forged close ties with its leaders, especially Huang, while removing constraints on the industry and opposing some new regulatory efforts.

In a recent development, at the same time, Trump has defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick against accusations of slow-walking export controls on China, the fiercest competitor in the AI race. And while Trump recently discussed AI during an in-person meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, he appeared to deliver few demands and achieved few assurances about Beijing's efforts to acquire U.S. chips.

"To say we can't do AI safety because of China, and then also be actively loosening the controls on China, makes no sense," McGuire mentioned.

Some of Trump's fiercest allies have raised similar qualms.

Industry observers note that "Reinstating Jensen Huang is going to blow back on our national security," MAGA activist Laura Loomer wrote in an X post Monday. "Eventually there has to be accountability for jeopardizing US national security. China didn't just get access to Nvidia chips by accident.".

Newt Gingrich, the influential former Republican speaker of the House, in an X post after Huang's reinstatement, wrote, "Congress should really dig into this as a national security glitch of enormous proportions and also a significant failure in the federal bureaucracy.".

Their criticisms sharply contrast with the praise coming from Silicon Valley and some of the Trump-friendly voices within it, such as Elon Musk, who wrote Monday, "The mistake has been corrected.".

But that's a shrinking political constituency, McGuire said.

"The tech-right perspective is very out of touch with where most of the Republican Party is on these issues, to say nothing of the Democratic Party," he said.

"Those positions are just not going to be sustainable for much longer," he added. "I think they're already becoming unsustainable.".

#2750. Porsche 718 Boxster prototype drive: This electric roadster is real

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1319 w)

Porsche 718 Boxster prototype drive: This electric roadster is real

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1319 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It wasn’t until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche’s upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is.
  • Recent findings suggest that that’s not particularly low for a sports car, but it’s practically unheard of for an EV.
  • So, for the firm’s first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It wasn’t until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche’s upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle.

Recent findings suggest that that’s not particularly low for a sports car, but it’s practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that’s usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed.

So, for the firm’s first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to fresh heights of power and performance.

It has been revealed that that EV battery layout, stacked behind the two-seat cabin rather than sandwiched below it, isn’t novel. It’s the same setup that Tesla used on the original Roadster back in 2008. Back then it was done for cost reasons as much as anything, enabling Tesla to repurpose a Lotus chassis meant to hold an internal combustion engine in the middle.

For Porsche’s new Boxster (and the Audi Concept C, which is built on the same platform), that pack enables the low seating position and also delivers a rearward weight bias (40:60 front/rear) that’s in keeping with the last-generation 718 Boxster, the internal combustion model killed by EU cybersecurity regulations last year.

Porsche isn’t saying how big the upcoming roadster’s battery is in terms of charge capacity, only that its size was chosen to balance range and weight. We also don’t have an idea of rated range, charging speed, nor battery composition, but I can say the battery pack is based on an 800 V architecture like the electric Macan, so hopefully we can expect charging performance that at least matches that SUV’s 270 kW.

The new Boxster also shares a motor with the Macan. Porsche is not quoting any specs yet, but it puts out about 500 hp (370 kW) to the rear wheels on the Macan Turbo. You can place your bets on whether the Boxster application will result in more or less power. I would take the over, but regardless, it’s enough to sprint this electric roadster to 62 mph (100 km/h) in under 3.0 seconds, making it the quickest Boxster ever.

Recent findings suggest that but it’s also the largest and heaviest. I was told the new Boxster’s curb weight will be somewhere in the ballpark of a current-generation 911, so in the region of 3,300 to 3,700 pounds (roughly 1,500 to 1,700 kg), meaning it has gained at least a few hundred pounds. That’s light for an EV but heavy for a roadster. Its wheelbase has grown accordingly.

You can absolutely feel that on the road. The 718 just doesn’t have the same buzzy eagerness as the latest 718 Boxster or Cayman. But that doesn’t mean it’s less fun to drive. In fact, I think most people would say it’s much more fun. Nearly doubling the old car’s base power output will do that.

Industry observers note that this car, though, is about a lot more than acceleration. It still turns and handles incredibly well, borrowing much of its suspension, steering, and even chassis from the current-generation 911. Few would call a 911 a boring car, and the 718 is a step more aggressive even than that coupe.

Sources indicate that that’s in part thanks to the response afforded by the electric powertrain, which isn’t saddled by the lazy throttle application caused by turbochargers and modern emission regulations. It’s sharper even than the latest 911 GTS, which required a trick electrically assisted turbocharger plus a battery and electric motor to bring the EV feel to a car driven by internal combustion.

To bring some of the charm of internal combustion to an EV, Porsche followed in the footsteps of the Hyundai Ioniq 5N by adding synthesized shifting and engine noises to the mix. Many cringe at the thought of an EV wailing unnecessarily, but having driven many battery-powered machines that make gas-powered noises, I can say with assurance that they always dial up the fun factor.

It has been revealed that what they often lack is authenticity. Porsche sampled the sound of what its engineers determined was the sweetest-sounding 718: the 981-generation Boxster GTS. The latest 718 Boxster replicates both that car’s 3.4 L flat-six and its seven-speed dual-clutch transmission, controlled by the paddles behind the steering wheel.

Recent findings suggest that enable the system, which Porsche calls E-Shift, then put the Boxster into launch control, and you’re in for a bit of a show: The car not only sounds like it’s bouncing off of a rev limiter, but the car itself actually shakes. It does this by pulsing the electric motor, vibrating in much the same way that the original Harley-Davidson Livewire did.

Lift off the brake and the Boxster blasts forward, again doing the sprint to 60 in less than 3 seconds. All the while, the pretend engine is screaming and running through its mock gears, either automatically or at your command with the paddles. In manual mode, the car will hit that artificial rev limiter and abruptly stop accelerating, so you’d better be quick to grab that next gear.

This whole system is there to add a greater sense of emotion to the car, but it does serve a practical purpose. Slinging the 718 around the tight, twisty circuit at the Los Angeles Porsche Experience Center, I was better able to judge my speed through corners by listening to the pretend engine that sounded all the world like it was spinning happily behind my head.

Don’t like it? Press the blue button on the steering wheel and it all goes away, but I have a feeling most people will want it on, at least when they’re driving for fun. They will certainly want it on when cruising into their local Cars & Coffee, since you can hear the sound outside the car as well as on the inside.

In a recent development, cruising is better in the upcoming 718 than the older model as well. Its adaptive suspension, dialed down to Normal mode, handles concrete separation joints on the highway and bumpy roads without glitch.

It has been revealed that and it offers something extremely rare on the EV scene: true drop-top motoring. The top folds itself down in somewhere around 10 seconds, tucking itself neatly on top of that battery pack. It also offers reasonable practicality, with a frunk in the nose plus a decently wide if shallow trunk out back. Both are roughly massive enough to handle a carry-on suitcase or a couple of backpacks. That’s about it, though. There’s effectively no room behind the seats.

Recent findings suggest that so, from a lifestyle perspective, it’s a bit more flexible and a bit more comfortable than the previous-generation Boxster, and from a power and aggression standpoint, it’s on another planet. Still, there’s no hiding that increase in weight and wheelbase. This truly feels like a cross-breed between a Boxster and a Carrera, which will disappoint some purists, but if you had to pick a pair of parents for a upcoming model, you could do a lot worse than those two.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of users. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that newly introduced job listings on Apple’s website indicate the manufacturer’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the company has also introduced new restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple announced plans to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give users more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted new job listings that offer a closer look at its looks to develop autonomous AI agents:.

Industry observers note that in one, Apple remarked it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

Today’s report on the upcoming job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring users to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the company could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the newly introduced job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its intends for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how rapidly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally introduced its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that phones have gotten a lot more expensive over the last year or so, and it’s a trend we’re expecting to get worse before it can get better.
  • According to recent reports, while buying year-old hardware typically comes with some pretty deep sacrifices between generations, that’s not particularly true with the Pixel 10 this year.
  • So what are you giving up that matters?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that phones have gotten a lot more expensive over the last year or so, and it’s a trend we’re expecting to get worse before it can get better. If you’re in the market for an upgrade, this year’s Black Friday might be one of the final truly good times to buy a new device, and for just $600, last year’s Pixel 10 should be high on your list.

According to recent reports, while buying year-old hardware typically comes with some pretty deep sacrifices between generations, that’s not particularly true with the Pixel 10 this year. From a hardware perspective, nearly everything is either identical or close enough to not particularly matter. Its design and display are all but unchanged, Qi2-ready magnets come on both models, and both devices are built with the same level of battery longevity in mind. And much to the chagrin of many a Pixel die-hard, Tensor G5 and Tensor G6 are practically interchangeable.

So what are you giving up that matters? When the Pixel 11 arrived, software features made up the bulk of this list, but with last week’s Pixel Drop, a lot of the gaps between these two generations have been closed. Gemini Intelligence with Rambler, app automation, and more are in the process of rolling out to existing Pixel 10 owners, and latest features like Create My Widget arrived on the Pixel 10 and 11 at the exact same time. From a software perspective — Google’s bread and butter, in my eyes — the only substantial sacrifice comes from the year of software support that’s already complete, leaving you with just six instead of seven.

Realistically, the camera is the one place you’re likely to feel a difference. The Pixel 10 was the first non-Pro device in Google’s Tensor era to ship with a telephoto lens, but it came with some significant sacrifices. The main sensor is effectively an A-series lens, and taken together, the entire package might leave something to be desired. It’s far from a bad camera though — I used it as my main shooter through most of its lifecycle — and while the Pixel 11 did get some upgrades here, I think real shutterbugs would be better off looking at Google’s Pro lineup anyway. You’ll also lose out on things like HiLight, though really, are you missing that much?

According to recent reports, what makes this deal so good is really its place in the market, not as a direct comparison to the newer Pixel 11. For $600, Google’s competition is going to have a hard time competing with the value the Pixel 10 delivers. Hell, even Google might find it difficult to compete in the coming months; at full price, $600 is what the Pixel 10a goes for now, a decidedly less-impressive device compared to this model. No, this is a flagship smartphone through and through, and for $600, you’re effectively guaranteeing a reliable, powerful smartphone experience from now until 2032 — hopefully enough time for this whole RAM crisis to finally simmer down a bit.

The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks.

In the world of athletic smartwatches, it isn’t often that you could mistake one for a luxury watch, but Honor seems to want to flip all that on its head with the Honor Watch 6 Pro. Just take a look at this excerpt from the company’s press release:.

Framing this brilliant display is a Precision Nanocrystalline Ceramic bezel crafted through a 1400°C high-temperature integrated sintering process, delivering a delicate texture and rich visual depth.

Inspired by modernist architecture, its diamond-cut octagonal rotatable crown features a dual-layer horizontal and vertical cut, complemented by a side button for intuitive navigation.

That sounds pretty wild to me, and it’s backed up by specs that sound just as legit, too. On top is a 1.5-inch LTPO Tandem AMOLED display that outputs 5,500-nit peak brightness. Underneath is a bevy of newly introduced sensors called the Intelligent Sense System, which Honor says combines “multi-wavelength monitoring, multi-optical path patrol technology, and anti-interference glass technology to reach deep skin layers.”.

Recent findings suggest that runners will be pleased to know that the Honor Watch 6 Pro not only incorporates a dual-band GPS, but combines it with a “star-pointing 3-antenna design” and an AI fusion algorithm, which should deliver ultra-accurate tracking in any location and no matter how you hold your wrist. Despite its luxury looks, this one tracks over 120 sports modes, including Honor’s Professional Running Coach feature, which tracks running posture, lactate threshold, heart rate targets, and keeps you on pace with real-time voice coaching.

Recent findings suggest that during sports modes like Badminton, the watch can identify more than six types of swings, and Honor states other sports modes can deliver similarly detailed statistics. The watch is 5ATM, IP68, IP69, and IP69K water-and-dust-resistant rated, plus it integrates directly with Strava so you can pull all your fitness data together.

Honor is incorporating a upcoming wrist twist gesture system this time around, letting you use gestures to perform actions hands-free. The watch is rated at 10 days of battery life on a single charge in regular usage mode, while endurance mode will stretch that to 18 days. Pre-sales begin today, November 19, and run until December 31, when the watch is expected to launch, starting at €279/£229 for early bird pricing. After launch, the retail MSRP starts at €379/£329.

Industry observers note that if you've been thinking about buying a Kindle or another e-reader, you might want to take a look at this Android tablet before spending your money. The TCL NXTPAPER 11 Plus gives you a paper-like display that's designed to be easier on your eyes, but unlike a traditional Kindle, it can also do pretty much everything you'd expect from a regular Android tablet. And the best part? It's now available for less than $200.

The TCL NXTPAPER 11 Plus combines a paper-like display with the flexibility of a full Android tablet. It features an 11.5-inch 2.2K 120Hz screen, three display modes, 256GB of storage, and an 8,000mAh battery with 33W fast charging.

✅ Recommended if: You want a paper-like display for reading, prefer a larger screen for books and PDFs, or want an affordable Android tablet that handles streaming, browsing, and everyday tasks.

❌ Skip this deal if: You want the weeks-long battery life of a dedicated Kindle, prefer a smaller e-reader, or need a powerful tablet for demanding games and heavy multitasking.

According to recent reports, TCL has been making NXTPAPER devices for a while now, and the NXTPAPER 11 Plus is one of the more interesting tablets in its lineup. Unlike other NXTPAPER tablets, this tablet lets you switch between three different modes, including Regular Mode, Color Paper Mode, and Ink Paper Mode, simply by pressing the dedicated NXTPAPER Key on the tablet.

You can use the regular mode when watching videos or browsing the web, switch to Color Paper Mode for a more comfortable reading experience, or use Ink Paper Mode for a more traditional black-and-white e-reader feel.

Speaking of display, the NXTPAPER 11 Plus comes with a 11.5-inch display with a 2.2K resolution and a smooth 120Hz refresh rate. That noted, the best part of this tablet is probably its design.

Industry observers note that it is only 0.26 inches thin and weighs around 1.08 pounds. That makes it easy to toss into your backpack before a flight or carry around throughout the day without adding much weight. TCL has also given it a metal body, so you're not getting a cheap-feeling plastic tablet despite the affordable price.

Battery life shouldn't be much of a concern either. The NXTPAPER 11 Plus packs a sizable 8,000mAh battery, which should be plenty for long reading sessions, watching movies, or getting through a day of regular use. And when you do need to charge it, there's support for up to 33W wired fast charging.

According to recent reports, of course, there are a few compromises at this price. The tablet is powered by the MediaTek Helio G100 chipset, which isn't exactly a flagship processor. It's perfectly reasonable for everyday tasks like reading, browsing, and streaming, but don't expect the same performance you'd get from a more flagship Samsung Galaxy tablet or iPad.

That mentioned, if you're looking for a relatively inexpensive tablet this Black Friday that also doubles as an e-reader, this is probably one of the best deals you can get right now.

Just imagine you're an actor who booked an unspecified gig years ago and then found out nearly half a decade later that you were performing a role in the biggest video game of all time, Grand Theft Auto VI?

Pretty cool, huh? That's exactly what happened to 63-year-old Guy A. Fortt.

According to recent reports, and if you were Fortt, you'd probably want to proudly show off your scenes to your whole family and all of your friends. Right? There's one substantial problem for Fortt, though: He has no idea who he played in GTA 6.

And there's another concern for Fortt, who, according to IGN, previously had roles in both Jessica Jones and The Sopranos. He doesn't have an Xbox or PlayStation 5, so he can't even play the game and try to find his character(s).

It has been revealed that however, Fortt does have a Facebook and Instagram account. And he posted a video on both detailing his GTA 6 dilemma. Now, according to Fortt in a follow-up video, millions of gamers are essentially on an in-game scavenger hunt to find the character or characters that Fortt played.

"I was a motion capture actor on GTA 6, but I don't know who the hell I am,” Fortt explained in his viral Instagram video. "I auditioned about four or five years ago; they put the balls all over my body and face. And then I forgot all about it." Industry observers note that whatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp owners: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the latest limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the latest limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the update becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company announced four latest features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

Tidal unveils ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (603 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them.
  • Recent findings suggest that tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI.
  • According to recent reports, as things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal confirmed that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists.

Recent findings suggest that tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of newly introduced uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated.

According to recent reports, as things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it’s only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements.

Credit: Tidal Credit: Tidal.

It has been revealed that some people don’t particularly mind AI music, but the team at Tidal has come to believe the harm to artists is too great. AI models can pump out random noises faster than humans can create things of real value, which can mislead listeners and siphon royalty payments away from creators. There’s also an concern with AI uploaders who are actively attempting to steal royalty payments. Tidal states it has already removed about 66,000 tracks from its service for impersonating artists, which was against its AI policy even before this update.

Recent findings suggest that as of December 9, individual uploaders and distributors will no longer be allowed to add AI music to Tidal. However, they could lie, couldn’t they?

Tidal hasn’t specified how it detects AI music, but it will probably rely on watermarking. Almost every AI song on Tidal (94 percent) comes from Suno, which added watermarking earlier this year. Tidal also cites Google Lyria as a source of AI tunes, which has SynthID labels embedded in the waveform. Deezer claimed it has a licensable AI music detector with a false-positive rate of less than 0.01 percent, but it’s unclear if Tidal is using that or something similar.

In a recent development, that will take care of most AI music, but this approach won’t detect everything. There are open models for music generation that you can run locally on a GPU, and some cloud-based providers aren’t bothering to watermark their outputs. Even if Tidal is using a separate detection system, upcoming models may be able to evade it—it’s always going to be a cat-and-mouse game. This will be a problem with verifying provenance in all types of media in the future. For the time being, at least, Tidal’s policy should clear out most of the AI slop.

It has been revealed that the people directing robots to make these songs will have plenty of other options after Tidal blocks AI. Spotify, YouTube Music, Deezer, and Apple Music all allow AI music on their platforms with labeling. Spotify has removed millions of AI tracks from its collection based on user feedback. Other streamers haven’t specified how much slop (if any) they’ve cleared out.

The kitchen tap gets a workout over the holidays. There’s coffee to brew before everyone’s up, a pot of soup on the stove, and a pitcher that always seems to need refilling right as dinner hits the table.

Whether you’re paying closer attention to family health or simply want better-tasting water for coffee and cooking, Waterdrop Filter has options for different kitchens and budgets. Its Black Friday & Cyber Monday deals run November 19 through November 30, with savings of up to $700 on premium RO water filtration and more affordable everyday filters. Use code 9TO5MBF26 for an extra 5% off the five systems featured below, on top of their listed sale prices.

From a Waterdrop reverse osmosis system for a busy family kitchen to a countertop dispenser for a smaller apartment, here’s how to find a home water upgrade that fits your routine.

According to recent reports, the best under-sink water filter for your home depends in part on how many people are filling glasses and cooking at once. For families of six or more and frequent hosts, the Waterdrop X16 Alkaline Mineral Reverse Osmosis System is the flagship option.

Its capacity of up to 1,600 gallons per day helps keep water flowing when everyone’s getting ready in the morning or preparing a holiday meal. The 11-stage filtration system adds calcium and magnesium back after reverse osmosis for a more balanced taste, while the tankless design leaves more room beneath the sink.

The smart faucet lets you check filter life at a glance. The X16 is known for its fast dispensing and compact design. During the sale, it’s $1,299, down from $1,999, saving $700, or ~35%.

For a family of four or five, the Waterdrop G3P800 Reverse Osmosis System brings under-sink reverse osmosis to the kitchen for less. It offers up to 800 gallons per day, with 10-stage filtration, UV sterilization, and a smart faucet that highlights filter status.

Both systems have a 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio, producing three parts filtered water for each part sent to the drain. Waterdrop claims the X16 and G3P800 help reduce contaminants including lead, PFOA, and PFOS. Waterdrop also lists NSF/ANSI certifications for both models, covering reverse osmosis performance and lead content in the materials. The G3P800 carries additional certifications covering taste-related filtration and specific contaminant-reduction claims.

G3P800 is recognized for its straightforward filter changes and the difference it makes for water, coffee, and tea. It’s $699 during the sale, down from $999, for $300 in savings and 30% off.

If you’re shopping for a reverse osmosis water filter, countertop models make it possible to upgrade without changing the plumbing beneath your sink. Renters, apartment residents, and anyone who wants water ready for tea at the touch of a button may prefer a countertop RO system.

Recent findings suggest that the Waterdrop M6CG Mineral Hot & Cold Reverse Osmosis System combines countertop reverse osmosis, remineralization, and hot and cold dispensing in one appliance. Its 59°F to 203°F temperature range covers everything from a cool glass of water to tea, cocoa, and other hot drinks.

Five volume settings and a customizable Favorite Mode let you save your preferred temperature and serving size. There’s also a detachable 40-ounce glass pitcher you can carry straight to the dinner table, which is handy for family meals and holiday hosting. Separate feed-water and wastewater tanks keep the two apart, and the M6CG has the same 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio as the under-sink models.

The M6CG is $409 during the sale, down from $539, saving $130, or ~24%.

For a more affordable countertop water filtration system, the Waterdrop CT01 Instant Hot & Cold Water Filter Dispenser offers the same temperature range with six-stage non-RO filtration. It helps reduce chlorine, rust, and sediment while retaining minerals, and it produces no wastewater.

According to recent reports, like the M6CG, the CT01 requires no installation. Its 1.32-gallon tank means fewer trips to refill it throughout the day, whether you’re keeping water on hand at your desk or making another round of tea. For winter hydration, having hot and cold filtered water ready in one place is a convenient addition to the kitchen.

The CT01 is $199.99 during the Black Friday sale (20% off).

If you mainly want to improve the taste of the water from your existing tap, the Waterdrop TSA 8 Layer Under Sink Water Filter System is an accessible place to start.

It connects to your cold-water line and uses eight-stage filtration to help reduce chlorine, sediment, and other impurities. Replacement schedules vary by cartridge, from about six months for the pre-filter to as long as 18 months for the carbon block filter, depending on usage and water quality.

The TSA is $90.24, down from $119.99, saving $29.75, or approximately 25%.

For a simple step toward healthier hydration, choose the setup that fits how your household uses water. Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday offers run through November 30. Remember to use code 9TO5MBF26 for an extra 5% off the featured systems.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Tuesday struck a conciliatory and remorseful tone while leading his first employee meeting since being reinstated, and stated how sorry he was for what he had done.
  • Huang told employees that he let them down and promised to do a better job the second time around, according to people inside the room, who asked not to be named in order to share details.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Tuesday struck a conciliatory and remorseful tone while leading his first employee meeting since being reinstated, and stated how sorry he was for what he had done.

Huang told employees that he let them down and promised to do a better job the second time around, according to people inside the room, who asked not to be named in order to share details. "I hurt all of you," Huang said, according to one of the people.

According to recent reports, the CEO also addressed succession planning during the event, the people noted. He told staff that Nvidia has built a team that doesn't require succession planning the way a normal organization does, because the organization operates a unique business model where there are multiple capable leaders at Nvidia that are leading different parts of the organization.

A succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy, Huang said, according to one of the people present.

Investors and analysts were left to speculate about the manufacturer's future leadership in the wake of Huang's resignation on Nov. 12.

On Monday, Huang was reinstated as CEO of the chipmaker by Nvidia's board of directors. Eleven days before, Huang had resigned from Nvidia after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, stated last week that Huang resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the organization's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms.".

Huang started the meeting by thanking CFO Colette Kress for her leadership as interim CEO.

Sources indicate that huang told staff that Tuesday's company meeting was the second hardest meeting of his life, the first one being with his wife. He noted he is in therapy, according to one of the people present.

Sources indicate that in a press release announcing Huang's return on Monday, the company remarked the board "received input" from senior officials in the federal government about any potential national security risk around the CEO. President Donald Trump told CNBC that he gave the board assurances and "made the deal" to restore Huang to his post.

Recent findings suggest that after the tech giant had its worst week in the stock market since 2008, the stock surged more than 30% the day his return was announced. Shares fell on Tuesday, however.

An Nvidia representative didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area more than six months after receiving the permit that allowed the companies to pull the human safety driver from behind the wheel.

The companies will soon begin offering driverless rides to employees in the final lead-up to launching a commercial robotaxi service in the first quarter of 2027.

The milestone comes just 16 months after Uber declared an ambitious blueprint to launch a premium robotaxi service using Lucid electric vehicles outfitted with autonomous vehicle technology developed by startup Nuro.

In a recent development, that strategy came with hefty investments in both companies and much-needed endorsements of their respective products. Uber initially agreed to invest $300 million in Lucid — a figure that has since ballooned to $500 million. Uber also agreed to invest nearly $500 million in Nuro, TechCrunch previously reported, citing sources familiar with the deal.

In a recent development, the agreement provided both Lucid and Nuro with boosts beyond the obvious capital injection. Uber agreed to buy at least 20,000 of Lucid Gravity SUVs over the next six years, giving the struggling EV maker a more predictable source of revenue. Nuro, meanwhile, was less than a year removed from announcing a risky, but necessary pivot away from developing driverless delivery vehicles and toward licensing its autonomous vehicle technology to automakers and mobility companies.

Industry observers note that nuro has spent nearly a year testing the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area with a human safety operator behind the wheel. The California Department of Motor Vehicles, the agency that regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, granted Nuro a driverless AV permit in May 2026.

Uber and Nuro are also testing autonomous vehicles on public roads in Houston with human safety operators behind the wheel. Nuro is supplementing that on-road testing with closed-course testing and simulation to validate the self-driving system before opening the robotaxis to the public. The companies’ combined engineering fleet of autonomous vehicles, which stood at 100 AVs earlier this year, is expanding as Lucid begins manufacturing the first production versions of the robotaxis at its Arizona factory.

The Lucid Gravity robotaxi, unveiled in January 2026, is outfitted with high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar sensors, and radars that help the self-driving system perceive the real-world environment and operate in it. Uber, which will own and operate the fleet, has focused its efforts on the in-cabin experience, including how riders will interact with the vehicle.

  • In a recent development, iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how customers open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

In a recent development, iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

In a recent development, opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

One of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

You can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point owners toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

It has been revealed that apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the latest Siri experience.

In a recent development, the last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

In a recent development, now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

I've been always swiping from the left corner to see my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the center to get to it as well 😂 I guess I'm good then?

Sources indicate that apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri.

Industry observers note that after 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s newly introduced Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

After months of using the new behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

Recent findings suggest that what do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1383 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick mentioned Monday.
  • It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there.
  • Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick mentioned Monday.

It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there. In Utah, several lawsuits are still playing out, and Kalshi also lost a bid to persuade a federal appeals court to block those cases until the appeal is resolved.

Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading. At this time, the federal district court has not granted that motion to block Utah’s enforcement actions, either.

“This is an unfortunate outcome for the more than 177,000 Utahns who use Kalshi,” McGavick said. “We will continue to fight this in court, and we look forward to returning to Utah once our legal position is vindicated.”.

Utah’s attorney general, Derek Brown, had filed both civil and criminal charges against Kalshi, as he defended the state’s 130-year ban on gambling.

In a press release discussing the initial lawsuit, he accused Kalshi of running “an online casino” that violates the state’s constitution. “Not only do our state laws ban gambling but Utah is one of only two states where gambling is also prohibited under the state constitution,” Brown remarked. “For 130 years, Utah has been clear: gambling has no place here, and we will enforce our laws.”.

According to recent reports, late Monday, a major Utah-area news outlet, KSL.com, reported that Brown was prepared to jail Kalshi’s co-founders, who had been summoned to be booked on 14 charges on December 5. He defended those looks, saying, “There is a question I have seen from people asking, ‘Well, do we modify this booking process if someone is a very wealthy and well-known tech billionaire?’ and the answer is ‘No, the process is the process; we don’t modify it based on who you are.’”.

Recent findings suggest that however, on Tuesday, Utah decided to drop the criminal charges against Kalshi, McGavick confirmed to Ars. In a statement on X, Kalshi general counsel Yaakov Roth remarked, “We are pleased that Utah has chosen to dismiss criminal charges against Kalshi, while proceeding with civil litigation. Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized. We stand ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.”.

In a press release, Brown explained that the charges were dropped specifically due to the pause.

“Kalshi said it would geofence Utah, which blocks access to its site in the state,” the press release said. “The tech giant also committed to monitor for Utah-based IP addresses trying to reach its site. The Office then reevaluated its position and moved to dismiss the criminal case against the company and the individual defendants.”.

Brown threatened that the charges would be raised again if Kalshi tried to renew operations.

It has been revealed that “Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling,” Brown mentioned. Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges. Every company in this space should take note. If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.”.

Discussion of the Kalshi pause in a Utah sub-Reddit found some Redditors skeptical of the state’s cases as potentially overreaching.

In a recent development, however, many top commenters seemed pleased with the enforcement efforts, suggesting that Utah may have bipartisan support among some residents. One commenter cheered on the attorney general’s efforts as “the one item in the Utah GOP’s agenda I can get behind,” while another agreed that “prediction markets are incredibly toxic and are manipulated against ordinary people.”.

According to recent reports, many complained that Kalshi ads flooded their social media feeds. Some suggested the state should focus on banning advertising of prediction markets, while potentially still allowing adults to trade on event contracts if they want to throw their “money away.”.

In a recent development, fears of insider trading were also raised. One commenter laid out why prediction markets seem suspiciously designed to promote insider trading and other market manipulation:.

“I’m pretty libertarian and hate banning things. But gambling and prediction markets are a scourge. Even the term ‘prediction market’ is a misnomer. Because ultimately when people with major dollars get involved it creates a financial incentive for them to make fucked up things happen in the real world. Think about it, decades ago we understood that sports betting was a problem because it corrupted sports—something that ultimately is pretty meaningless. Then we got all these people betting on the stock market with puts and it created huge incentives to cause havoc with markets. Now if people are betting big money on politics and wars and everything else, it just means people with influence can make money by making improbable/unexpected things happen.”.

Sources indicate that one commenter joked, “I wonder how Kashi would have reacted if the judge in charge of their case had ‘traded’ $500,000 on the event of them losing the case. Not a problem at all, right?”.

On the same day Kalshi confirmed its temporary pause in Utah, a judge rejected a request from New York Attorney General Letitia James to immediately shut down Kalshi in that state, Courthouse News reported.

Latest York Supreme Court Justice Melissa Crane said she was “uncomfortable” granting the temporary restraining order so early in the case because “there does seem to be an indication that there would be market disruption that I’m concerned about.” Kalshi attorney Grant Mainland described it a little differently, claiming that a sudden halt would cause a “market emergency.”.

In a recent development, “I think this is the ultimate relief in the case, which is improper for me to do without full briefing,” Crane mentioned. Instead of granting James’ request, she recommended that Kalshi take steps to address the state’s top concerns by considering “safeguards for users between 18 and 20,” who are under the state’s legal gambling age, Courthouse News reported.

According to Kalshi’s estimates, Upcoming York’s Kalshi user base (1.5 million) is much larger than Utah’s, so the market disruption from the Utah shutdown may not have carried the same dire stakes for Kalshi or its broader user base.

The CFTC has sought to intervene in that case, too, and it seems clear that Kalshi expects the questions of who can regulate prediction markets and what trading qualifies as a “bet” to reach the Supreme Court. Kalshi’s spokesperson did not respond to Ars’ questions on how the Utah pause broadly impacted people or the platform.

So far, “three federal appeals courts have ruled that states can regulate prediction markets, while a fourth found they cannot,” Courthouse News reported. But despite the current balance tipping toward allowing states to regulate prediction markets, Kalshi appears confident that the Supreme Court will resolve the disparate court rulings in its favor.

In a lawsuit filed by a disgruntled Kalshi user, Kalshi argued that it would waste lower courts’ time to continue litigating these cases and that no case should be resolved until the Supreme Court weighs in.

In that case, Kalshi user Scott Bright alleged that he lost more than $300,000 on sports bets that were technically illegal in Washington.

Industry observers note that according to Kalshi, all of Bright’s claims rest “on the premise that state gambling laws reach KalshiEX’s federally regulated exchange—the question now before the Supreme Court. Plaintiff puts the cart before the horse; Defendants ask only that the Court let that threshold question be resolved first.”.

The court has yet to address Kalshi’s request to stay the case, but Bright has argued that Kalshi is trying to “sideline a case governed by binding Ninth Circuit precedent so that they can wait for a Supreme Court decision that may never come.”.

Kalshi did not respond to Ars’ request for a statement on Bright’s lawsuit. In their court filing, they argued that “a stay will let the Supreme Court address an glitch that could dispose of every claim, will not meaningfully harm Plaintiff, and will spare Defendants and the Court litigation under a framework that may soon be displaced.”.

Android's sideloading freedom is about to get a lot more complicated worldwide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For quite a long time, Android has had one big advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission.
  • Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the manufacturer.
  • Recent findings suggest that confirmed in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For quite a long time, Android has had one big advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission. That freedom is about to come with considerably more friction.

Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the manufacturer.

Recent findings suggest that confirmed in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed. The new rules will also apply to third-party app marketplaces and independently distributed APKs.

Google is working with seven distributors, including Google Play, Samsung’s Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo, to bring the requirements to more customers.

Industry observers note that google indicates the changes are intended to make it more difficult for scammers and malicious developers to continue distributing harmful apps. The company says millions of applications have already been registered, representing more than 99% of Android app installs worldwide. The launch began on September 30, 2026, in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.

Industry observers note that but developers won’t be the only ones feeling the shift. To install unverified apps, you’ll have to take extra steps. You’ll have to authenticate your device and make sure you’re not being forced to change your security settings. After this, restart your phone and wait 24 hours before you can enable unrestricted sideloading.

Google does offer an advanced install option for power customers who want to skip verification, but it’s not quite the one-tap experience Android enthusiasts have grown accustomed to.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

There are also concessions for smaller developers. Free limited-distribution accounts allow students and hobbyists to share apps with up to 50 authorized devices without having to verify their identity with a government ID or pay registration fees. Google has also added APIs to make it easier for developers with multiple apps to register.

But the bigger question is what this change means for Android’s reputation as an open platform. Google says users can still choose where they download their apps from, but the freedom is made a lot less convenient by adding identity checks, restrictions on installation, and a mandatory waiting period.

After the global rollout, protections are expected to be available to all countries and installation sources over the span of a few months. Google documentation states that full enforcement is expected on March 1, 2027.

  • Tidal remarked it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year.
